item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports distinguishing observed feedback from inferred intent, but the search found no established taxonomy matching all four requested labels. A defensible audit would label immediate endorsement, deferred interest, explicit mismatch, or unidentified content, attaching an exact feedback span and item identifier; keep identification certainty separate from preference. Treat this as a proposed annotation scheme. [Sources of Disagreement (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.comedi-1.3/) shows that task formulation and annotator choice change instance-level labels even when aggregate agreement remains stable. Double-annotate supplied feedback, report agreement and class confusion, and adjudicate ambiguous examples. Calibrate abstention against adjudicated labels using error-versus-coverage curves; [Contrastive Decoding with Abstention (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.479/) supports explicitly evaluating whether available evidence warrants an answer, although it does not validate this recommendation taxonomy.\n\nFor GRU diagnosis, [TimeSHAP (KDD 2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073) provides recurrent sequence attribution, while [Demystifying Sequential Recommendations (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) studies minimal history edits that change recommendations. An applicable audit would compare original histories with paired recent-event deletions, older-context deletions, or order changes, preserving left padding and final-nonpadding readout. Measure candidate-score/rank changes alongside hidden-state changes and embedding gradients; verify attribution with deletion tests. These probes establish model sensitivity, not users’ causal motives or definitive component responsibility. Ground interpretation only in supplied feedback, histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; leave ownership, compatibility needs, and latent traits unknown without explicit evidence. Apply probes to each category’s single trained GRU model; retain macro validation HR@10 for selection."}
